spec_match.rationale: Built directly from the §10.5 precision note (banding visualisation with code-value counts), the unclamped-color() contract (real out-of-range declarations with computed readback), and the color-gamut media feature.

interactive.rationale: A bit-depth slider redraws the double ramp and recomputes gamma-vs-linear code-value counts; a probe button runs three real declarations; the gamut readout updates live on media-query change events.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises visible banding, out-of-range behaviour and display-gamut reporting — all three stages exist.

edge_cases.rationale: This is the edge-case angle: precision loss, unclamped components, and hardware gamut limits, with the pre-144 rejection branch printed verbatim and the srgb-linear row showing the live unclamped contract.

conformance.rationale: Suite assertion out-of-range-components-parse pins the unclamped contract this page demonstrates; suite verified executing on /conformance/.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable here): desktop screenshot read — the linear half of the ramp visibly bands coarser at 6 bits; DOM shows '34 of them; raw linear-light gets only 16', the computed unclamped color(srgb-linear 1.5 -0.2 0), and the three gamut query results; CDP clean console, no overflow at 360.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts banding-ramp-drawn with the code-value counts, out-of-range-parses-native or -unsupported-fallback, and gamut-reported.

design_system.rationale: Token chrome; the JS-illustration badge is amber-on-amber-border with ivory text; the greyscale ramp is the demo content.

accessibility.rationale: The slider is a native range input with visible label and live value; the ramp canvas has role=img with a description and its findings are duplicated as aria-live text with numbers; probes are keyboard buttons; gamut output is role=status.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Slider width caps at min(280px, 70vw); CDP-measured no horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3; both class screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate float-backed rendering removing the banding once linear canvases are testable
openQuestions.detail: The natural follow-up pairs this page with the Chrome 155 canvas feature: an srgb-linear canvas with colorType 'float16' should show the bottom ramp without banding. Needs a 155 runtime with ColorSpacePredefinedLinearSpaces; link across to the v155 feature when built evidence exists.

guidanceConsulted.query: range slider accessible label visible focus
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Native range inputs with programmatic labels, visible values and focus indication.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The bits slider is a native input inside a visible label with a live value span and aria-describedby pointing at the numeric findings; focus-visible outline defined.

guidanceConsulted.query: canvas redraw on slider input jank
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep input-driven canvas work cheap enough for the input frequency.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The ramp is a single 640x120 putImageData recomputed per discrete slider step (7 steps), well under frame budget; no continuous animation runs.

summary: Edge/failure concept: makes the spec's precision warning visible as gamma-vs-linear quantization banding with real code-value counts, probes the unclamped color() contract with verbatim computed values, and reports the display's true gamut live. Verified in headless Chromium 141 at both device classes with clean console.
